ideas.main_idea: Using underwater soundscapes to monitor coral reef health
insights: We have six years of hydrophone recordings from 40 coral reefs across the Pacific.
Healthy reefs are louder and more acoustically diverse than degraded reefs.
Bottleneck: we have no reliable way to automatically classify fish calls; manual labeling covers less than 1% of the audio.
Looking for machine learning audio classification that works with very few labeled examples.
ideas.raw_text: (synthetic) How can I classify thousands of hours of reef audio when only a few hundred clips are labeled?

ideas.main_idea: Tracking coral reef recovery after bleaching with acoustic indices
insights: Acoustic indices may not track fish abundance reliably.
Need long-term field data on coral reef recovery after bleaching to validate the acoustic indices.
ideas.raw_text: (synthetic) Is the acoustic complexity index actually correlated with fish counts?

insights: I developed a contrastive pretraining method that learns audio features from unlabeled recordings.
Our few-shot audio classification models reach good accuracy with as few as 5 labeled examples per class.
Most audio benchmarks are speech and music; I am looking for large real-world field recordings to test robustness.
ideas.raw_text: (synthetic) Which nonspeech audio datasets are big enough for pretraining?

ideas.main_idea: Robustness of audio models to environmental noise
insights: Audio classifiers degrade badly under background noise such as wind, rain or boat engines.
Experimenting with augmentation that simulates environmental noise.
ideas.raw_text: (synthetic) How do I simulate rain noise for augmentation?

ideas.main_idea: Thermal tolerance of corals during marine heatwaves
insights: Running heat-stress experiments on Acropora corals to find heat-tolerant colonies.
Symbiont shuffling may help some corals recover after bleaching.
We have eight years of field monitoring data on coral bleaching and reef recovery on the Great Barrier Reef.
ideas.raw_text: (synthetic) What explains variation in bleaching recovery between neighbouring colonies?

insights: Diver surveys of reef recovery are slow and expensive.
Looking for cheaper automated ways to monitor coral reef health continuously between surveys.
ideas.raw_text: (synthetic) Are there sensors that can monitor a reef continuously?

ideas.main_idea: Population coding in mouse visual cortex measured with two-photon calcium imaging
insights: We record calcium imaging from thousands of neurons in mouse visual cortex during natural movies.
Struggling to infer spike times from noisy, slow calcium fluorescence traces.
Need better statistical deconvolution of calcium traces, with uncertainty estimates for spike inference.
ideas.raw_text: (synthetic) Why do my inferred spikes change so much when I change the deconvolution parameters?

ideas.main_idea: How behavioral state changes visual responses
insights: Running and arousal change visual cortex responses.
Pupil tracking used as a measure of arousal.
ideas.raw_text: (synthetic) Should I regress out running speed before decoding?

ideas.main_idea: Bayesian state-space models for noisy time series
insights: I develop sequential Monte Carlo methods for latent state inference in noisy time series.
Expertise in Bayesian deconvolution and uncertainty quantification.
Looking for real scientific datasets with thousands of parallel noisy time series to apply these methods.
ideas.raw_text: (synthetic) Can particle filters scale to thousands of parallel series?

insights: Variational inference can scale state-space models to thousands of parallel time series.

ideas.main_idea: Open-source pipeline for calcium imaging analysis
insights: I built an open-source pipeline for motion correction and cell segmentation of calcium imaging data in zebrafish.
Spike inference from calcium fluorescence traces remains the least reliable step in our pipeline.
We benchmark spike inference against simultaneous electrophysiology recordings.

insights: Light-sheet microscopy lets us image the whole zebrafish brain during behavior.
